Power Strip with USB, VASTFAFA Flat Plug Power Strips 6 Outlets and 2 USB 4.5Ft Extension Cord, Multiple Protection Wall Mount for Home/Office, UL Listed(White) It’s only smart to use a surge protector for all electronic devices. And while this unit may not protect your devices from a direct lighting strike it will definitely protect from fluctuations in current.

This 6 outlet, 2 USB surge protector is easily mountable using the 2 included screws. I simply placed the bottom on my printer / scanner and hit copy - that provides an exact mounting template. Following that, tape the piece of paper where you want to mount, pre drill small pilot holes through the paper marking where your screws go, remove paper, insert screws, mount.

The 2 USB (2.4A each) easily accommodates most USB plugs and self regulates charging speed to charge your devices at the fastest possible speed.

There are 6 surge protected, 3 prong outlets. The farthest one to the right is offset to provide room for larger brick style plugs.

I mounted mine to the underside of my laptop desk next to the couch and it has operated perfectly.

While the box shows that the power button illuminates a blue color when on, it does not. I checked with the manufacturer and that is not a defect - there is no LED light there. Not a big deal.

This would be the perfect surge protector / outlet strip for next to the bed, taking on cruises or other locations where you need extra outlets and protection from electrical fluctuations.

text_fidelity_a:
BSIMB Digital Picture Frame IPS Display, Wall-Mountable Electric Photo Frame with Remote Control, Place in Landscape&Portrait, Gift for Grandparents Frame is a tad slow to respond to the remote; that could be better. It isnt always slow, just sometimes it doesnt pic up, other times it is fast & perfectly fine. I think it has to do with distance from frame. Dont be too close!

They have a large frame with touchscreen available, so I would personally go with that unless price dictates otherwise. I like the remote too, just wish it responded faster and more consistently. I wouldn't want just a touchscreen. Option for either/both in one would be cool. Anyway.. I like this. It is my first frame. I have been kind of using our Echo Show, and sometimes just a computer screen. But I have wanted a basic frame, so here I am.

Basically plug it in, get it on the network, get the app, make an account, pair with phone, then select pics off phone to be loaded. Can choose up to 50 at a time. Very easy. Surprisingly so. I am tech savvy but impatient. This was pretty easy to figure out. Takes a few minutes to get them loaded.

Picture quality is quite good, and occasionally looks off. Thought that might be original source rather than the frame. All considered, all pics are quite clear and detailed.

if you have it set to full screen, then some pics may be cut off. If you have it set to the other option (cant remember the term), then the pics come up as you took them. Glad I figured this out because at first I had some that were cut off and it made me sad. Got it fixed very easily and all is well. YAY

Can set up calendar, weather, location, an alarm, play music, load videos. Can set time and make it a clock, can choose clock face. Can choose 12 hr or 24 hr format. Can create slide shows, decide on length of time, random or sequential or based on when taken. Very cool. Oh, and even incorporate music. Can label/add words/text too. Easy on, easy off.

Can operate basic stuff directly from the frame. Including very quickly rotating a pic. No need to use remote for everything!

Has headphone jack on back

It really isnt bad as an entry level frame. Would be nice as a gift if preloaded for someone. Now that I have been using this, I know what to look for in an upgrade. But this will certainly make do as i get to know it more and more. Ive only been playing with it for a day or so. The more I write about it, the more I like it.

I think pics can be emailed to this like Skylight subscription frame. Can let other people add photos.

Can also add photos/music/video via a SD/MC/SDHC, USB, USB mini, or thumb drive.

Needs to be plugged into wall receptacle.

Says in one of the product pictures that it can be wall mounted . I dont see how. It is a landscape mode item with a back portion to help it sit upright. It would not ever be flush with wall. I wouldnt buy it for that anyway. I got it for use on a side table so I can see pics of my dogs and cats all day long.

text_fidelity_a:
Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black The need for an uninterruptible power source is obvious to anyone with a computer or other expensive electronic equipment. The very day this product arrived, before I even opened the box, a severe thunderstorm knocked out power in my neighborhood. My two computers immediately went down and the screen on one kept flashing on and off even after all the power was dead. So yes, a UPS seems like an important piece of equipment these days. Sadly, this one is not for me. To be fair to the manufacturer though I need to give you a bit of context to help you evaluate if my reaction and this review would be applicable to you or not.

At age 70 I have a pretty low tolerance for muss and fuss. If it requires special handling, if it is a hassle to use, I don't want it. If it's not plug and play, I won't bother with it. For example, I do all my laundry in one load throwing everything in together without any sorting of any kind. It all gets washed and dried on the hot cycle. Anything that can't handle that gets tossed out. I treat everything like that. This UPS looks like an industrial strength product but acts like a delicate little snowflake. Coming out of the box it has 20 pages of instructions they want you to read before using. I didn't bother, just plugged it in, turned it on, and starting using the USB charger to juice up a battery run children's night light. A little while later I noticed a burnt plastic smell and saw the warping on the case that you can see in the attached photos. So this thing is not for me. More detail oriented and careful folks might have better luck with it. Thus I'm giving it a neutral 3 star rating and suggest you read through all the reviews here before deciding whether you want to try it yourself or not.
text_fidelity_b: Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display Pros:
-Easily programmed.
-Multiple game memory.
-Many, many keys = many, many programming options.
-Digital readout looks good and lets you know exactly what download you are using without reopening Logitech window.

Cons:
-Flat palm positioning is not very comfortable for gaming (and can't be adjusted). My hand tends to cramp due to its bad ergonomics when playing FPS games more than an hour.
-Keypad ergonomics are badly thought out. Key rows are positioned bowing UPWARDS (away from your fingers) instead of downwards, making quick initiation of pinky and index finger keys more difficult.
-G13 is a bit large and can't easily be slid aside when not gaming (not a big deal to me, but somewhat inconvenient).
-Friends tell me that Razer and Logitech downloads interfere with one another, so if you have a Razer mouse or keyboard this may interfere with your use of either.
-Keys are a bit too close together without easily discernible gaps in between. This too often causes my thick fingers to strike 2 keys simultaneously.
-Overpriced for what it offers.

Overall:
Programming=excellent. Ergonomics=horrible.
For me, the keypad layout and palm rest do not work together. They look like they should, but they simply do not. The device concept is quite good, but the ergonomics make it just too difficult to consistently access and manipulate keys for real-time gaming. Very disappointing to me because with Logitech's years of experience in peripherals this should put Nostromo to shame---it simply doesn't because of the badly positioned keys and faulty wrist/palm rest ergonomics.

Follow-up:
-Down from 2 to only 1 Star, and it should be ZERO Stars. This thing is good only for a paperweight to remind me of my wasted time and wasted money.
-6 months down the road and, while gaming, each and every one of my gaming profiles (I have 3) will spontaneously reset to the default profile on their own or, even worse, all the G-keys become unresponsive.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the LCD screen lights up, but no profiles appear, not even default, and no keys respond.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the unit never powers on.
-Logitech's updates do not fix the problem(s). I've deleted the entire gaming software setup and performed reinstalls ad nauseum with no permanent positive result. What's even worse is this: it acts fine for a bit after a reinstall, so you think you've corrected it, then it starts screwing up ALL OVER AGAIN.
-BIOS adjustments do not fix the problems.
-USB ports and motherboard are completely functional throughout my gaming (I've tested/monitored them as I play) and they perform perfectly as the gamepad and/or its software crashes on its own.
-It's only 6 months old, and 2 keys are mechanically non-functional (G20 and the button below the joystick). My Belkin Nostromo n52 lasted for almost 8 YEARS of gaming with no problems whatsoever, and I was gaming three times as much back then. I'd grown used to the G13 so I was willing to overlook the buttons, or blame them on myself, and work around this issue, but when the software/electrical issues began occurring quite regularly I'd run out of patience.
-Forums addressing these (as well as other) issues have found no answers or solutions, only make-shift quick-fixes.
-Numerous forums also share the information that this is happening across a variety and multitude of different computer systems/set-ups.
-Many other owners, myself included, have had additional problems with the G13 when it is used after a computer has hibernated/slept, but we all learned to live with this as one of its quirks. We now see this as an indicator of its many issues.
-Many other owners have said that the problems began occurring after 3 or more months use (I suspect that in my case this took longer as it is only occasionally used for gaming).
-Logitech customer support has denied any fault in these matters and still maintains that their pruduct and programming is NOT the cause of any of these problems, so their help line has been useless. Meanwhile, the price plummets as word spreads.
-Only thing that works for any of us is to constantly disconnect gamepad from its current USB port, reconnect it, and computer may recognize it...but this does NOT always work...sometimes requires reboot as well...and sometimes this doesn't work either...so gamepad is inoperative until it decides to come back on a reconnection or restart. This is a band-aid at best. I refuse to do this to my system over and over.

This thing is getting returned. I advise you to save your money and time by buying some other manufacturer's product.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display

text_fidelity_a:
SPARIN Galaxy Tab S3 / Galaxy Tab S2 9.7 Screen Protector - S Pen Compatible / Tempered Glass / 2.5D Round Edge / Scratch Resistant / Easy Install for Samsung Galaxy Tab S3 / Galaxy Tab S2 9.7 Inch Crystal clear, fits well, and is very light weight. Honestly, I was a little nervous about buying what I perceived to be a cheaper product online. However, the idea of paying 40+ dollars to have a screen protector applied to my screens always seemed outrageous to me. So I figured I'd give it a shot and after reading the reviews for several products, I decided to give this Sparin a shot and ordered one for my Galaxy Tab S2.

Placing the screen protector on the S2 was painless and quick. A few quick wipes with the wet and dry clothes provided and a few moments centering the screen protector over the tablet screen. Put the stickers on to hold the screen protector in place, peel off the backing, and put it on the screen. No joke, it's pretty simple. So simple that I managed to somehow mess it up.

What resulted in me messing the up install and quickly attempting to fix is soon resulted in two corners that would not stay down. "No problem," I though, since the screen protector is designed to be re-applied several times. However, after one or two attempts, and with now two corner sticking up, I was resigned to having a screen protector that just sticks up.

As a last resort, I contacted Sparin support. Despite a small hiccup with email addresses, I quickly heard back from support. They provided a few useful tips to apply the screen protector and to attempt to get the corners to stay down. Ultimately, the tips did not work. Again, I was going to be stuck with a screen protector that sticks up.

Not so! As it turns out. Sparin did not hesitate to send me another screen protector. No questions asked. No photos requested. Not subject to verification. Just a quick reply from Sparin apologizing for a bad experience (which I will admit is mostly my fault), and that a replacement was already in the mail - it is! - and with that, they earned a very loyal customer.

I cannot say the product is poor, because it's not. I have no doubt this protector will keep my screen free of scratches. However, my attempts to install it were lackluster. There's a reason we paid trained teenagers at the mall to install these things for us.

Luckily for me, this great product is backed up with amazing support.
text_fidelity_b: SPARIN Galaxy Tab S3 / Galaxy Tab S2 9.7 Screen Protector - S Pen Compatible / Tempered Glass / 2.5D Round Edge / Scratch Resistant / Easy Install for Samsung Galaxy Tab S3 / Galaxy Tab S2 9.7 Inch

Renegade Concepts: Lap PRO - Stand/Caddy Universal Beanbag Lap Stand Tablet Accessory for iPad 1, iPad 2, iPad 3, iPad 4, Acer, Nexus & All Android Tablets, E-Readers, Books & Google Devices (Blue) The LAP PRO universal tablet stand doesn't work very well with my Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Wi-Fi tablet. The stand consists of a very firm, 18-inch wide, cylindrical pillow with a soft handle that doubles as a sort of tray for the tablet. Because there is no frame to hold the tablet securely, the tablet must be set carefully into the handle-tray, and then the tablet simply leans against the pillow for support. However, the tablet is very easily dislodged from the tray, even when the stand is sitting on a flat tabletop.

Out of the box, the LAP PRO holds the 8.9" Kindle Fire HD tablet at a near-vertical angle that is uncomfortable for viewing or for using a stylus on the touch screen. There is a sheet packed with the pillow that says: "Your LAP PRO has come slightly over filled intentionally, which may interfere with some functions. This will change in time. This is to ensure it will perform properly and last longer after it breaks in. The fabric will stretch and the beans settle from use." However, this is not really a beanbag stand. The pillow is filled with something that feels like medium-fine sand (not beans). Also, the pillow is too firm to accommodate its shape to an uneven surface the way a beanbag does.

To adjust the tablet viewing angle, you must reshape the pillow--it isn't enough to simply roll the pillow forward or backwards. Because the pillow is so firm, you must exert some effort in reshaping. It is easier to adjust the pillow shape and the viewing angle if you unzip the zipper that runs alongside the handle-tray, but then the pillow kind of flops around. (The zipper is there to open and close a compartment that is probably intended to hold your tablet, because the LAP PRO is also supposed to be a "caddy".)

If I needed a travel pillow (another of the LAP PRO's advertised uses) or a tablet caddy, I might end up liking the LAP PRO. However, because the stand is too large for convenient tabletop use, is hard to adjust, doesn't hold the tablet securely, and needs break-in time, I rate it at 2 stars ("I don't like it" on the official Amazon scale).

EDITED 11/18/12: After hearing from the seller, Renegade Concepts, I believe that I may have received an overfilled LAP PRO. (Renegade Concepts offered to replace my unit.) If my LAP PRO had been less firm out of the box, I would have rated it at 3 stars ("It's OK").

text_fidelity_a:
TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405 Was hesitant to buy a not so known brand. However for the most part its a really good TV. Did some research on TCL and found out that several tv brands were in fact manufactered by TCL. Emerson, RCA, Phillips etc.

I did pay extra for a entended warranty because the last 2 tv's I owned both went to the recycle bin in about 2.5 years. However, the extended warranty for parts and labor worked out to be about 10$ a year. The Insurance company figures that the failure rate isnt going to be that significant based on how low the cost for the warranty.

The remote and the menus on the TV dont have much functionality. I guess Roku thought that having a more plug and play approach would be better. The app for your mobile device has that functionality though. Can change picture settings etc. I have yet to find the sound options though. Be aware that going to external speakers via audio out also cuts off the internal speakers. Picture quality is really good overall. There are times though that it appears to be trying to upconvert to the 4K from a lower definition video stream and when it does there are some interesting visual artifacts. I don't know why but I think that some streaming services have encoded the audio of their content differently due to needing to increase volume on TV from say 35 to 95 in order to hear it. As a example Netflix volume on tv 35 to 40.. Amazon prime I have to increase volume to 90 or higher to achieve same level of hearing as Netflix. There are variations of course but generally speaking over the entirety of the video libraries of both services thats what I have to do. Blue ray is fantastic through TV.

I do have several years experience with roku streaming devices and those do work well and I have never had a hardware failure in them. I would suggest setting up a roku account before initializing TV. Makes setup way easier.

Havent been able to notice a difference between wired connection and wired as far as visually or sonically.

Overall, for a 55 inch class TV for the price.. Decent deal. Will have to see how the hardware lasts.
text_fidelity_b: TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405

text_fidelity_a:
Altura Photo Camera Accessories Bundle - Photography Accessories Kit for Canon Nikon Sony DSLR & Mirrorless Cameras, Includes Small Tripod for Camera, Lens Cleaning Kit & Camera Cleaning Kit My daughter and I do a lot of photography of jewelry. We have had a variety of tripods and camera aids. This kit seemed like a good one for us. I got it.

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
CASE
This has a hard case that zips around the edge. It has a pocket in it to hold things in place and a cupped side to allow for the tripod storage.

LENS BAGS
There are bags in here which fit small medium or large lenses. I don't have any lenses yet, but I do have a small light that fits in one.

CLEANING CLOTH
These come in a zip topped plastic bag. This is pretty nice and works well as is expected with microfiber cloth for cleaning glass.

QUICK RELEASE CAMERA STRAP
This comes in a nice package with good instructions in it. The idea is that this helps stabilize the camera when you are taking a lot of photos. You can not have to grip the camera so hard so your hand does not get tired too. If you accidentally slip your grip, it does not crash to the ground.

This had a learning curve to it, but I finally figured out how to use it for me where it was helpful.

LENS PAPER
This paper allows you to clean the lens off gently wet or dry. The wet means that you use the Altura cleaning solution for greasy heavier prints.

PUFFER CLEANER
This is a rubberized ball that when you squeeze it, there will be a blast of air that will blow things off of the lenses. This works quite well when I get a particle on the lens so I don't have to touch it.

BRUSH
This is when the dust won't blow off the lens or other glass you can gently brush it and then blow it away with the puffer cleaner.

EMPTY BOTTLE
This is for alcohol or lens cleaner.

TRIPOD
This is why I wanted this kit the most. It has an ingenious design to it. It folds up flat and quite small, yet when you take it apart and tilt it, you can stand it up for close photos, or use it in your hand. It has rubber on the bottom to keep it put, and it also has a rubberized grip if you want to hold it. The camera platform tilts, but it locks into place which I love. This is working great for us taking close up photos of some of the small jewelry we are photographing. It has come in really handy.

What I love is that we can pick it up and use it by hand if we need another angle than the table top one.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This kit is a nice kit. I got it mostly for the tripod, but the cleaning accessories and the wrist strap make it really nice. The puffer ball is one of those things that you don't realize you need until you have it.- at least for me. The case is protective and easy to travel with.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am happy with this kit. It has worked better for us than I expected. We will be using this a lot in the future too.
text_fidelity_b: Altura Photo Camera Accessories Bundle - Photography Accessories Kit for Canon Nikon Sony DSLR & Mirrorless Cameras, Includes Small Tripod for Camera, Lens Cleaning Kit & Camera Cleaning Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Eversame Bundle of 3Pcs/lot Multi-color 6 FEET 2M Fabric Braided Nylon Ruggedized Micro USB2.0 Data Cable Durable Universal Charging Cord For Samsung Galaxy S4 S3 S2 Note 1 2 4 Tab HTC ONE M8 X NOKIA Lumia PDA X-BOX Motorola, LG Optimus G3, PS4 and Most Android Tablets/Android Phones/Windows Phones (Black White Pink) Most of the USB cables I have are either 3' cables or are really short ones that come with electronic devices. Sometimes a longer cable is really handy, especially when the immediate area surrounding a work space is cramped. I looked to these 10' cables to help alleviate one such issue and I learned a few things. One of those things is that a cable can be too long in some cases, though this is a failure in organization, not in the cable.

These are flat USB cables. Flat cables are less likely to tangle than their round counterparts, but I will confess to preferring round cables anyway (it’s a personal preference, not a technical preference). These are shielded in woven nylon which is great; the nylon is stronger than soft plastic shielding and gives the cable a little more stiffness but does not make the cable so stiff that it’s awkward to run. The connectors are interesting - two-tone plastic that is different than anything else on my desk which makes it a lot easier to determine where both ends of the cable are plugged in. I tried stressing the cable ends at the connectors by trying to pull out the shielding from the plugs and they held firm.

I tried one of these with my phone and it worked just fine, I was able to charge the phone and move data between it and my laptop. I did not attempt a speed test.

There is a big difference between 3' cables, 6' cables and 10' cables. If you need a 6' cable, a 10' cable will leave you trying to figure out what to do with the extra 4' of cable. In my case this meant having to use a twist tie to bunch the cable up in the middle. This is not a criticism but rather a suggestion - get a cable that’s the right length for the job. If you need a 10' cable, these have worked great for me.

These are nice USB cables. They seem to be made well and they work as expected. If you need a really long cable, this is a good choice.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Eversame Bundle of 3Pcs/lot Multi-color 6 FEET 2M Fabric Braided Nylon Ruggedized Micro USB2.0 Data Cable Durable Universal Charging Cord For Samsung Galaxy S4 S3 S2 Note 1 2 4 Tab HTC ONE M8 X NOKIA Lumia PDA X-BOX Motorola, LG Optimus G3, PS4 and Most Android Tablets/Android Phones/Windows Phones (Black White Pink)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) July 27, 2018 - update. To preface, let me say that my previous Fire tablet was with me for just under 5 years, is still working fine except that it doesn't hold a charge as well as it used to (which is why I went with a new one). This tablet I've had since February so we're talking 5 MONTHS instead of years. As of today, the screen is cracked. Since I don't carry it with me the way I used to carry the previous one, and since the case I have this one in is sturdier than the previous case, and since, to the best of my knowledge, this hasn't been dropped, I'm not pleased. I'm thinking this probably arrived this way, since the crack can only be seen when it is a just the right angle to a bright light. Of course, it won't be covered under the "limited" (that should read VERY limited) warranty, and apparently, I failed to buy the protection plan because I was thinking this was as well built as my previous Kindle. Wrong on all counts. So I will say that it just went down to a 3 star review, partly for the company and not just the Kindle. For all the trouble I had with the books and being able to read books I'd purchased, this was the last thing I expected to happen. If I buy another reader, since I've already figured out I don't like Amazon knowing everything I do through Alexa, it won't be a Kindle.

February 2018 - I just received my new Fire 10 last week. I am moving from my old Fire 8.9, because the battery had decided not to keep a charge, and I was lucky to get 2 hours out of it at one time. Terrible for traveling or using it where there wasn't a plug in available.

I had an unholy amount of problems with the Kindle books on my Fire 10. First once all 1300 books were downloaded, an awful lot of them, at least 20% were unreadable, because of a DRM error. Kindle support did a fine job of straightening that out, although it cost me about 2 hours on chat before it was completed. Then, some books didn't download when they should have so it took what seemed like two days to get them all organized and downloaded. But finally that was straight.

My next problem was with Alexa, whose answer to me is normally, I'm sorry I don't understand. But if the television is on, she apparently can understand the Olympic announcers because she responds to them right away. Because she responds to other voices, once at a restaurant this week, I have to turn her off when we're in public. Obviously, she's far too friendly with strangers. I had heard that this would be a problem, just didn't think it was going to be mine.

I am not a technophile, I can only tell you as an average person using this Fire tablet for all sorts of activities during the day, that it is functional, quick, and works very well with the apps I have loaded. I use my Fire far more that I'll ever use my phone for reading, purchasing, browsing, so I'm very pleased with how it operates. I like the size of the screen, I like the weight. I did not buy Amazon's cover for it, which I'm finding might have been a mistake, but I'll deal with that after the tablet and I have bonded. I can honestly say that when my 8.9 new it didn't work this quickly, so color me pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Zen X-Fi 8 GB Video MP3 Player with Built-In Speaker (Black/Silver) Zen X-Fi 16GB review 2-28-09

Had the Zen X-Fi 16GB for two months of daily use now.

The device is well built and solid. It needs a silicon skin for protection, though. That is extra but highly recommended so your expensive player doesn't slip out of your pocket.

First, the buttons are too flat and are not illuminated. Sounds like a small thing, but flat black metal buttons against a black metal background in the car at night are very difficult to find and press. If the buttons were transparent and had the tiniest LED behind them, they would be a lot easier to manipulate accurately.

No Bluetooth--I'm getting very tired of wired connection to my car and headphones. LOSE THE WIRES, Creative! The earphones that come with the Zen are terrific. Really good quality. But the wires are tiresome.

Though I'd rather have Bluetooth, Zen is Wi-Fi capable. You can wirelessly hook to your computer's wireless router and play or copy files back and forth, but it's so frustrating to make it function it's virtually useless. USB cable is the way to connect.

As part of Wi-Fi, Creative does provide something called "Media Server" that you can access via your internet connection wireless router if you're in range and properly connected. After waiting a couple of minutes for the connection to be made, you can listen to propaganda from all kinds of politically correct content like NPR, the BBC, Australia's ABC and KCRW. Yes, master: I hear and obey. Mostly a waste as you can't really select content you want, only what they supply. Definitely politically correct. And boring.

It has a kind of chat texting capability but that's what phones are for these days and the Zen's dinky keyboard just doesn't cut it. The keyboard is laid out the way it is so it can emulate a phone keypad when you're in chat mode. Too frustrating to use. It's why QWERTY keyboards are on phones now.

Bookmarks. A few minutes after being shut off, the Zen forgets where you were when you shut down. If you fire it up an hour after shutdown or dock it to your computer to upload new content, it starts playing the last file you opened from the beginning. This is a bit frustrating when you're part way through a three hour podcast. So Creative allows you to set a Bookmark from within the file you are playing. It's quick and easy once you figure it out. I use it all the time now. This allows you to set a point in a podcast so you can return to it later. But while you can set the bookmark from within the file, you have to navigate to the Bookmarks screen to select the bookmark when playing back later. Not very intuitive. Took me two months to realize the usefulness of the feature. Why doesn't it simply remember where I stopped listening by itself? My DVR does. Just resume from where I left off. But no.

The lower left button is programmable. It's called My Shortcut. You pick from a list of available functions and set it. This allows you to go to a particular favorite screen or function once you decide what that is.

The Zen first and foremost is marketed as a video and MP3 player. What I wish it could do is have a "skip forward" ability (again, like my DVR does) that allows me to skip forward 30 seconds or a minute (or a user defined amount) so I can move forward in predictable amounts instead of holding the fast forward button down. If it's going to be called a "player" of any sort, it should have a variety of player controls. Skip forward/back should be available. Firmware upgrade wish, Creative.

Speaking of the fast forward button, the longer you hold it, the faster it goes. It starts by forwarding at a slow rate, then speeds up until you are jumping forward minutes at a time. This is good for zooming to a point quickly. But if you want to go forward, say, seven minutes, holding the FFwd button down too long will launch it into hyperdrive and you'll be at 10 minutes or more into the file, then have to rewind/search back. Somewhat of a pain. No. A real pain. Let me skip forward or back in 30 second increments.

A great feature is its built-in speaker. It sounds like my transistor radio from my childhood. This feature was the main reason I bought the Zen: you don't have to use earphones if you don't want to. It is a great and rare feature among MP3 players. A pocketable mini boombox.

Creative's Centrale "iTunes wannabe" software is dreadful. I tried it for awhile, then uninstalled it and now just drag files to the device.

Video screen quality is very good but 320x240 is still a bit small. Diagonally it's 2-1/2"; 2" wide x 1-5/8" high. It's also the old 4:3 aspect ratio, not the modern 16:9. If you're viewing a 16:9 video letterboxed, you are looking at one tiny video.

The video player (as opposed to the music player) is very weak. Windows Media Player 11 it ain't. Another key reason I bought the Zen is because it promised it could play a plethora of video formats. Wrong. I have dozens of wmv video files which exist in many sizes and bitrates from thumbnails to HD. Unfortunately, almost all of them need to be converted via Creative's stand-alone converter app or Centrale into squeezed-down bitrates and 320x240 size. This process is clumsy and slow.

If virtually every file needs to be converted in order to play, it's not really playing the advertised list of formats: it's playing the format Creative has selected and must be converted to. Often, even if I render out a wmv directly from my video editing software to Creative's parameters, it still won't play properly without conversion. Yet another marketing promise dashed to pieces.

The Zen allows me to delete files directly from the Zen if I want to (as opposed to needing to plug into iTunes to delete or add). This is good.

It has a built in mic and audio recording capability and you can program the "My Shortcut" button to start the recording process immediately so you don't have to navigate to the recorder's controls.

It has an FM radio that only works if the ear phones are plugged in because the wire becomes the antenna. What I'd really like is an AM radio, though, for news, talk radio, traffic and weather. Who needs FM? That's what your MP3's are for in the first place, right?

The unit has an SD card slot, but it's not well integrated. Content on the SD card does not appear in the normal file list. You must navigate to the card and browse it separately. Worse, when you do that, it comes back with "There are no playable files in this folder" even when I know I put mp3 files on the card that the player can play. You have to use the "Import" function to move files from the SD card to the player's memory in order to play them. Think of the SD card as an aux thumb drive, not as expanded memory, except it doesn't even work like that, actually. If you think you can buy the 16GB and "double" its memory capacity with a card, think again. It's more of a gimmick than a useful feature. More Creative fluff that is long on promise but short on delivery.

By the way, when you plug the Zen into your computer's USB cable the Zen does not mount as a drive (what Windows calls a "Local Disk.") It "docks" as a "Portable Media Player" according to Type in Windows Explorer. This means you can't play directly from the player. If you click on a file on the Zen from within Windows, it moves the file to a temp folder on your C: drive before playing. Not a big deal, but if you intend on connecting the Zen to a USB input on your car stereo or computer, I don't think your stereo will be able to see the Zen's contents. While the Zen is docked to the computer, all the play buttons are disabled and the display indicates "Docked" until you unplug the device. On the other hand, you don't have to unmount the device. Just pull from the USB and go.

Poor Creative. Always trying. Never quite getting there. Won't be long now and a phone will do it all. Look at Sony Erickson's W760, iPhone or Palm Pre.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Zen X-Fi 8 GB Video MP3 Player with Built-In Speaker (Black/Silver)

Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home This headset does cancel noise, and the sound is clear. That part is fine. For the not-so-fine parts: they're really tight, and they cancel noise almost too well.

The tightness:
Right away, I felt that they squeezed my ears too much. I left them to stretch across several hard-bound books for a few days which loosened them up for a while, but they eventually go back to their original tightness that I can't wear them for more than 15 minutes at a time. My ears get squashed and they hurt to leave on, and I don't even have a big melon head!

The noise-cancelling:
While they do block out outside noise, they cancel my own voice out too, and I feel like I'm talking into a blanket by myself - I can barely hear myself talk. It's very disconcerting.

All in all, if they weren't so darn tight, I think I'd like them better. I had to dock 1.5 stars because of the physical discomfort, and .5 star for the talking-into-an-echoless-void factor. The sound quality is good, though. So, if you have a smallish head, and you like having all the outside sound shut out, they may work for you.

text_fidelity_a:
OhO Audio Sunglasses,Open Ear Audio Sunglasses Speaker to Listen Music and Make Phone Calls,Water Resistance and Full UV Lens Protection for Outdoor Sports and Compatiable for All Smart Phones Let's get one thing straight right away: THESE ARE NOT SUNGLASSES. They are blue-light blocking at best, or just mildly tinted most likely. I took them out of the box and thought "Oh cool! These are the kinds of glasses that get dark outside and transparent when you are inside!", but nope- I wore them for a full hour outside and they didn't get any darker or exhibit any sun blocking properties AT ALL. So that's false advertising right there. They aren't for use in the sun. They don't darken anything.
As far as audio quality... they are a cool concept, but again, falls short of expectations. The open ear design means the speakers have to work harder to be audible. That means they often make those tin-sounding rattles that tiny speakers make when cranked up too high. This is definitely NOT cool for music as most of the fidelity is lost right off the bat, and adding insult to injury is that they often don't get loud enough to use outside. I'm not saying using it in a crowded subway terminal (that you can just forget about completely), I'm talking about even just going for a stroll around my suburban block with some birds chirping and the wind blowing lightly, maybe a car driving in the distance. I tried listening to a recorded lecture (since music was a lost cause), and they couldn't get loud enough to hear clearly. The microphone for calls was OK in my test, so I guess they are cool as a way to take a phone call without wearing a headset, but that only works if you're wearing these anyway as sunglasses. They aren't sunglasses, so you wouldn't be wearing them anyway, and you wouldn't be wearing them for music, and you wouldn't be wearing them to make a phone call either because they rarely get loud enough unless you are home alone... in which case you can put your phone on speaker and avoid this whole mess.
In conclusion- its a good idea but executed poorly and does NOT live up to expectations. I'm surprised there are so many good reviews on this product. I can't think of a time I would use it.
text_fidelity_b: OhO Audio Sunglasses,Open Ear Audio Sunglasses Speaker to Listen Music and Make Phone Calls,Water Resistance and Full UV Lens Protection for Outdoor Sports and Compatiable for All Smart Phones

Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter I wanted to hear and see Skype on our Sony XBR7 HDMI-only capable 1080p TV, fed from a Lenovo X220 convertable laptop/tablet running System 7 64 bit Ultimate through the DisplayPort. I also wanted to watch some YouTube videos playing from Firefox and hear their audio on my big living room audio system. No such luck.

When first plugged in, I remember briefly seeing the TV via this DisplayPort adapter in the audio device list, but the next time, the TV disappeared and is nowhere to be found. Not in the audio control panel, anyway. It's just gone.

I first chalked this up to the Thinkpad weirdness, as its internal audio card/mic doesn't work with Skype either. If I plug in an external Logitech webcam, it works seamlessly. Internal camera/mic, nothing.

Sony audio problems aside, the video looks great on the big screen, though it overscans a bit and cuts off part of the menu bar at the bottom.

One reviewer said he could see his TV in the list of audio devices and was able to configure its audio to satisfaction. My Sony TV does not show in the Lenovo audio devices list, though it does show as a generic PnP monitor.

I plugged the HDMI cable into a tiny 7" video monitor and whatdayaknow, the audio came through and the device showed up as an audio device. Then I plugged it into a 20" Vizio and sure enough, it works fine too. Same with a Samsung LCD. Three monitors out of four work. The Sony is the only one that doesn't. Hmmmm.

Sooooo, I'm guessing there's something about Sony's DRM or some other HDMI protocol blocking the computer from seeing the TV. I set all the TVs for internal speakers. Routing audio to an external amp is another variable in the equation.

Nothing wrong with the adapter that I can tell, it simply doesn't see certain Sony TV's.
text_fidelity_b: Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Universal Smart Battery Charger Mark II For AA AAA C D 9V Li-on Ni-MH Ni-Cd Rechargeable Household Batteries With USB Charger Cell Port More than anyone, I really wanted alkaline charging to work like other rechargeable batteries but the sad reality is that they're just not made for it.

The reality of alkaline charging:
- Duracells seem to leak more than cheapo "Kirkland" brand from Costco.
- Energizers do not hold charge very well.
- All brands leak eventually.
- Takes a long time to charge.
- Unreliable even if successfully recharged -- usually, batteries are connected in series, which means that if one fails, the device will not work.
- Battery leak can happen while charging or while being used in the device, resulting in a very messy charger and messy device.

So after some dumpster diving (or at least, I raided the battery recycling bins at work), I came home with batteries of various brands. For a while, I really did use recharged alkaline batteries exclusively and kept my Ni-MH batteries in the drawer. What I found was that I needed to change the batteries a lot more often and I couldn't be sure that the battery would have a charge when I took it out of the drawer.

Leaking is a big problem. My charger now has one charging port that is stuck because the liquid got in to the spring mechanism and dried. I also have a couple of remotes and devices that had to be cleaned out because the batteries leaked.

In the end, I had to give up on the idea of recharging cheap alkaline batteries because of how long it takes to recharge and that it can leak at any time, potentially ruining your device (mostly, it's just oily and you need to clean it out with a tissue). I just couldn't trust those batteries.

So why did I still give this charger 5 stars? Although alkaline charging was a failed experiment for me, the charger is still a better-than-average Ni-MH battery charger. It has separate intelligent charging and LCD display for each battery and will trickle charge a battery even after the lights turn green. Other chargers that have the same features cost more -- and without the Alkaline charging capability. You really can't go wrong with this charger.
text_fidelity_b: Universal Smart Battery Charger Mark II For AA AAA C D 9V Li-on Ni-MH Ni-Cd Rechargeable Household Batteries With USB Charger Cell Port

text_fidelity_a:
Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens 50% FOV increase at this price? This is the lowest priced Plössl I've ever seen and the reason for choosing it. Curiosity.

As a physicist with a too time-consuming career to fool around with optical Garage-a-Tronics projects, it's time for fun. After >40 years, I'd guess 1/3 of my time was in electro-optical systems. My responsibilities included one of the nation's most sophisticated optical design, fabrication, and 50-200 layers of Å thickness vapor deposition coating capability (200 layers is no limit … simply the most I've seen engineered)

You have to give them credit. Chinese optics are extraordinary and have been for 20 years. Asian pricing has wholly changed the marketplace. The crazy low prices have made complex systems affordable to the mass market. Optical grinding facilities remaining in the US are confined to a handful of custom, proto-typing houses run by old-timers with a decidedly different product application than consumer use.

The Plössl eyepiece is quite expensive to manufacture given the nature of the glass, coatings, and its precisely coordinated concave and convex lenses to neutralize internal reflections.

The Plössl has tradeoffs. All optical systems do. For example, Plössl's increased FOV comes with an eye relief confined to 70–80% of focal length.

Lenses are analog. Performance is not binary. 'Lowest price' in optics might be misunderstood. Optics lots begin production targeted at a spec performance that makes a profit. A production lot will yield a normal distribution to spec. On the upper end of the distribution are a few 'blue diamonds' commanding a super premium. Theoretically, 66%, will meet the target spec. Production lots begin life as profitable, spec-centered customers. 7% would be expected to fall short of some spec performance (i.e. start 107% of what you need) … Harvard MBA's demanding perfection in all things except stock value have never come to terms with normal analog distributions in scientific endeavors.

The lenses come without ref to detail specs, so I would believe the factory is emptying the shelves of sub-spec product here. Spec fallout, in my experience, may have little or nothing to do with operator perceptions of performance.

Excellent fun.

Was my review helpful? If so, click "Helpful" so I can know. Trying hard to put integrity into reviews
text_fidelity_b: Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens

TP-Link Deco Mesh WiFi System(Deco M5) –Up to 5,500 sq. ft. Whole Home Coverage and 100+ Devices,WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Anitivirus, 3-pack This review is for the TP-LInk Mesh WiFi M5 system.
—————
Amended April 28, 2020
Now that I’ve been using this for a couple weeks, I am returning to add these units HAVE NOT cured the dead spots that needed more signal strength. Yes, the WiFi signal is present in those areas of my home. However, the signal strength has not improved over what my centrally located router produced on its own. Essentially for my roughly $125, I got a couple stylish WiFi access points. What I DID NOT GET is the improved coverage promoted in the description.
—————
This IS NOT a plug it in and it works system. You need to know at minimum:
—Your current router’s IP address, the user ID for it, and the password. If you haven’t changed them from the default, you have no business installing a network anything, because you put EVERYTHING on your system at high risk for hacking. Why? The problem is that the default user ID and password are the SAME FOR ALL routers of the same brand (every brand router has a published default user id and password).
—You need to know which of several comm protocols your ISP uses.
—You need to know that IF YOU SWAP OUT YOUR ROUTER for one of the units, the others WILL NOT WORK to extend your WiFi network. For that you need to set these up as extenders, with the first being connected to your existing router.
—To set up a network of WiFi extenders, you need to know how to turn your existing router’s WiFi transmission off. Only then can you use these as extenders, satellites, or whatever you know them as.
—You are highly likely to have to update the firmware on each M5 device.
—You should set aside about two to three hours to set up a network of multiple devices.
—If you set these up as extenders, some of the default security features are switched off. You need to be sure these security features are enabled on your router instead.

I found this an unacceptably under-documented product that forces you to comb through the internet for proper setup tips. I loathe their little booklet that is “documentation” since it is a collection of single pages in multiple languages that direct you to the App Store or Google Play for the app that manages setup. That app is underpowered, has little relevant or helpful information.

I’ve been working with and installing systems from early (1990s) mainframes, Apple IIs, Macs, PCs of all flavors, and networks right up to now. Were it not for that experience, I might never have gotten this to work. Once installed, it works fine.

Recommendation: If your current router is older, you’re probably more likely to get better WiFi coverage by purchasing a newer, more current router. Try that first, and if you don't get the coverage you need, add a couple or three of these.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Deco Mesh WiFi System(Deco M5) –Up to 5,500 sq. ft. Whole Home Coverage and 100+ Devices,WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Anitivirus, 3-pack

64G Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, Mp4/Story Player, Music Player, Supports FM Radio of High Volume Built-in Speaker, 4-Inch LCD Full Touch Screen, E-Book, Micro SD Card Slot Ups to 512GB (Black) It does what it's sold to do very well. I've tested several types of ebooks (PDFs, epub, doc, txt), mp3 files of various quality, pics, and vids (avi, x264, and x265) - it read and ran everything well and smoothly.
Basically it's a low-end phone running an old distro of Android. It's super locked down and there's no internet access, so there's no updating and no adding of apps - this includes bluetooth tethering. That being said, a few of the apps are ones I've used for ages and (obv) I like them: specifically moon reader, the ebook reader - it really works well on this device. And I believe the video player is MX Player, also an old fav. Moving files via TF card was a bit of a pain, as the older version of android only supports up to 4GB at a time, but otherwise it moved everything without error. I tested the reader with several cards, from a generic 32gb to a samsung 512gb u3, and they all read well, so you can easily have a large library of media at hand. There's no cam or wifi; and there aren't any sensors, so it can't tell tilt, ambient light, etc. The screen is tiny but looks surprisingly good. The speaker is decently loud, but it def sounds like a phone speaker, still though, it's better than expected.
If you just want a simple media device with some neat features (FM works really well btw), this is great. I both would and wouldn't recommend this for kids - you can't add any educational apps (or games, lol), and they wouldn't be able to access things like their school portal or wiki; but if you only want your kid to have books, vids, and audio with a few tools (calc, calendar, alarm), this is right up your ally. Heads up though, they can swap out the TF card if they have a media collection you don't know about, and Moon Reader supports requiring passwords for opening the app.
If you want something you can do more with, I'd suggest foregoing the 50% off coupon and getting a burner phone at this device's list price. A burner probably won't work as smoothly (because it will have more hardware/software), but it'll have wifi and an app store and updates.
I plan to use this as an extra/backup media device. I'm one of those weird people that has a TF collection in my bag with tons of movies, tv, games, etc. I'm going to put one of those pockets on the back for credit cards, and use a TF card organizing card to hold my cards, so I'll have all my media together and with a device that can play them, in case my phone is AWOL or dead. IMO, after the coupon, it's worth the price as long as you know what you're getting.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout) I purchased one of these 9th generation Kindle Oasis. The first unit I received would freeze during the configuration process. You could reset it, but if you try to configure, it would freeze again. At this point, I made the mistake of asking for a replacement instead of just returning the faulty Kindle Oasis for a refund. A replacement unit arrived in three days. Unfortunately, the replacement unit was DoA. There was a fixed image on screen, and I wasn't able to get a response from this Kindle after charging it for a long time and multiple reset attempts. I had already shipped the first unit back using a UPS shipping label created by Amazon at this point. I went to my Amazon Orders page to return the second unit for a credit. But Amazon web interface wouldn't allow a self service return for refund. I had contact customer service and deal with several customer service representatives. They consistently asked me to try some simple trouble shooting steps ( most of which are not even applicable if you have a completely dead kindle). They wouldn't listen to me when I said I just wanted to return it, and try to pressure me into another replacement. At this point, I had spent several hours troubleshooting, talking to Amazon Customer service, taking packages to UPS, etc. so I insisted on a return for refund. This time, the customer service representative said he was having problems generating the return label, and then disappeared. After several minutes of wait, another customer rep took over and worked on this case for another 10 minutes or so. At that point, I ended up with two sets of return labels in my email. The customer service rep told me to use the labels from the second email (in chronological order). So the next day, I shipped the replacement Kindle Oasis back. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the package was delivered to Amazon and three days after this I received an email confirmation from Amazon that my first return was received. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the second Kindle Oasis (replacement) was also received by Amazon. I waited a few days for return confirmation and refund from Amazon, but nothing happened. When I contacted Amazon Customer service, they kept telling me that I shouldn't worry about getting charged as my replacement is complete. But they could see no record of my return of the replacement. I spent probably a good half an hour chatting with a customer service rep but they couldn't help me at all since they could only see the record for on return request. That chat ended with no resolution because I ran out of time and had to get to an appointment. Later, I got in touch with yet another service rep, and explained everything from scratch. Luckily, that person was able to find records of both returns being received by Amazon and finally issued me a refund.

So lessons from this story:
1. Don't buy a 9th gen Kindle Oasis. There seems to be serious quality control issues. The probability of one customer receiving two faulty Kindles in a row would be infinitesimal unless fault rates are in the 20% range.
2. If you receive a faulty Kindle from Amazon, return it for a refund. Don't ask for a replacement. Amazon's automated return process cannot handle the return of a replacement unit, and you will sink a lot of time dealing with customer service representatives
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout)

I have a true split keyboard which I love in one work location and had a standard keyboard in another which has been replaced with this new one. The wave design will take some getting used to but it is definitely more comfortable to use than the standard. I have found the zoom buttons on the left side to be very useful. The application switcher is something that I am not sure that I will use. I tend to use Alt+Tab when I need to switch applications. I may end up programming that button to do something else. I do like the fact that with the Word Function key I can program that to open a specific folder that I access frequently to hold my in-process documents.

About the only thing I do not like about this keyboard is that it does not sit on all four feet. I've tried using all the angle options and still the keyboard rocks. From what I can tell the keyboard is just formed/molded in such a way that it doesn't sit flat on a surface with all four feet touching. This doesn't affect the use of the keyboard or mouse - it just one of those things that I noticed and that annoys me.

Update 1/29/2013: I noticed today that the keyboard no longer rocks. I am not sure why - the work surface hasn't changed but since it was the only annoyance I had with this product I thought it was important to come back and update my review.

I don't use all the buttons on the mouse (left, right, scroll up/down) so I can't comment on the usabilty or function of the other buttons. The mouse is smooth to work and I like the fact that there is a compartment within the mouse to store the USB receiver.

A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat8 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin package contains the needed shielding and wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

I used this 10’ cable to run from my router to my NAS - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription I’m really picky when it comes to mice. I usually end up with a gaming mouse because they are comfortable and fulfill my needs. But because I use a Mac, it’s rare that I can customize buttons and macros and all that.

So I was really excited to try out the Logitech MX Master 3. I’ve been using it for the past month and keep going back to it. I have two work spaces in my house, and I find myself taking the mouse from desk to desk, instead of using what’s already on the desk.

The mouse feels nice in my hand. I have small hands (size small in gloves), and the mouse nestles nicely against my palm. My fingers don’t have to stretch to reach any of the buttons. The thumb rest is comfortable. I only wish the mouse had better pinky support.

The scroll wheel … I love the scroll wheel. Logitech calls it the “MagSpeed™ Electromagnetic” scroll wheel which is a really fancy way of saying it scrolls like butter. The wheel is nearly silent and super precise. It has just the right amount of feedback when scrolling slowly through a page, and flies when I want to get to the bottom of a long article. It really is a joy to use.

The mouse charges via USB-C and includes a USB-C to USB-C cable. I couldn’t try out the Flow option, where you can copy/paste text, images, and files between computers because my other Mac’s version of iOS is too old to install Logitech Options. But I was able to connect the mouse to both of my Macs and switch between them using the 1, 2, 3 button on the bottom.

Logitech Options offers a decent amount of customization. You can customize settings across all applications, such as pointer and scrolling speed. Some of the buttons can be customized: gesture, scroll wheel click, wheel shift, horizontal scroll, back, and forward.

App specific options can be assigned to the buttons. Defaults are assigned for the most popular programs like Chrome and Photoshop, and I was able to add customizations for my personal favorite, Scrivener.

But what I don’t like is that I’m limited in picking what the buttons can do. I really wanted to change the horizontal scroll wheel into another vertical scroll wheel, but I can’t. I can only do the functions Logitech thinks I want, such as zooming or navigating between tabs.

The MX Master 3 has a lot of nice functions and has been designed for productivity. I’ve barely touched on a lot of what you can do with this mouse.

I just wish I could customize *everything* because what I need for productivity doesn’t match what someone else needs, or what Logitech assumes I want.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription

Its slim profile. But it will still hold a lot of gear.

text_fidelity_a:
RIVA TURBO X RTX01B Premium Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (Black) My first Bluetooth speaker was the Bose Soundlink; I then transitioned to a smaller, more portable Braven LUX. As an audiophile, when I was offered the opportunity to test drive the RIVA Turbo X, I jumped at it. The first thing I noticed right off the bat is the WEIGHT; the speaker clocks in at nearly 6 pounds (compared to the lightweight Braven, or the slightly heftier Soundlink). It's also designed like a sportscar, with a glossy black finish with red rubber accents covering access ports. The top contains streamlined buttons for Power, Surround, Bluetooth pairing, mute, up and down volume, and Turbo mode. There's also an iOS app that allows you to control the surround and turbo settings directly from your phone.

I appreciated the quick start guide handily attached to the top of the speaker; it recommends that you play the speaker at 50% volume for several hours to break them in. It comes out of the box partially charged (around 40%) meaning you can start using it immediately (which I did using David Garret's new "Explosive" album). The sound balance is fantastic; as I live in an apartment, unfortunately I'm not able to really take advantage of the Turbo mode (which boosts to over 100dB). Pairing was a snap and I was off and running. As soon as I synched with my iPad, I was prompted to download the "Ground Control" app (which as previously mentioned, gives you battery life stats, volume, and the ability to turn on surround and Turbo modes).

It also comes loaded with extras in the form of RCA cables, male-to-male audio cables, and it's also capable of charging other devices. The battery is recharged via AC (the life is around 26 hours); no USB option here. The touch buttons on top illuminate when you hold your hand over it, which is a fantastic feature in a dark room or if you're using this outside.

The sound is fantastic with just about every genre I threw at it, from Baroque opera vocals to instrumentals to EDM.

This is a serious investment that not only looks fantastic, but sounds absolutely fantastic...and my Bose Soundlink is going in the closet. If you're looking for maximum power with no trade in sound quality (especially at higher volume levels), the Riva TurboX is the way to go.
text_fidelity_b: RIVA TURBO X RTX01B Premium Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (Black)

APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately) this has nothing within Amazon's control! I have used APC UPSs at work for years and found them dependable, reliable for my 350+ server environment. Maybe their quality control doesn't extend to their consumer product line. upon install and following all instructions the battery failed self test, really!?!? it was manufactured 9/2103 passes their internal QA per document included in package but fails 3 months later????

update: 1/27/2014
did chat with APC support. I was told I should have plugged in UPS and charged battery for 16 hours PRIOR to attempting to put a load on it. NOTHING I have read in the accompanying documents even hinted to that. I am skeptical, but will do as instructed for process of elimination in troubleshooting this problem. I told the support rep that this little bit of information should be passed on to the END USER SOME HOW!! I will update this review as I go through the resolution of this issue.

update 1/29/2014
So I did what APC said and took the load off and charged the UPS for 24 hrs (I figured a little extra wouldn't hurt). Installed the UPS and placed a load on it (~35%), performed the self-test and it passed. This KEY IMPORTANT fact should be SOMEWHERE in the included documentation, it would help everyone! I did increase my rating since the product now works as described, not happy about the lack of documentation and extra hassle required kept my ratings from being higher.

Samsung Galaxy 5.0 Android MP3 Player Pros: Bought one of these refurbished for my 10 year old son. I read a terrible review on Cnet and man is it wrong. This is not a tablet but can act like one and it is not a phone, but can act as one with the right app. It is a great Kindle or Nook with ereader apps. It has expandable memory unlike a Kindle Fire or Apple anything. It will still fit in your pocket. The screen is great and not grainy at all. It is very similar to a Galaxy S 2. Video play back is better than any of the similar priced iPod touches because of the larger screen. The camera is very good as well. If you are tired of iTunes problems, this is your device. You plug it in and it becomes a hard drive and you drop your music on. No crazy iTunes and I have 5 Apple products in my house. I love my iPad. I hate iTunes and the whole restoring your iPod errors that my kids experience.

Cons: None

Other Thoughts: This is a great player and is not a true tablet or phone and should not be compared to either, yet it can function as a tablet, movie player or even as a phone. Plus, it is a great gaming device and best of all, no iTunes to mess with. Set it as a mass storage device and off it goes. Also, It is a great ereader. FYI,the CPU is single core but plenty fast. The video gpu is faster than the iPod 4's. If you like Galaxy Phones you will like this a lot. I am not sure what motivated the Cnet review I read, but it was terrible.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy 5.0 Android MP3 Player

Dislikes.

I wish it was smaller. It’s much larger than I expected. Make sure you have enough room.

Overall.

The bluetooth connection.
I set the radio to bluetooth, then went to bluetooth settings on my IPhone. The IPhone immediately recognized the radio, and paired. I played both songs and the Audible books, using this connection. I ordered the radio in order to listen to hours of Audible books at night. I usually fall asleep while listening, and it played throughout the night. That way, I wouldn’t be exhausting my IPhone battery constantly, as it uses a lot less battery life, when it doesn’t need to pump out volume. text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory I'm normally an ear bud user since I've never been able to find an over the ear headset that was comfortable to wear for more than 10 minutes or so at a time. Well, I found one - these are undoubtable the most comfortable headphones I've ever used. Just a dream to wear even for extended periods of time. Light, cushy, just right. And they look so elegant - a nice change from the sparse industrial look that electronics often have.

Construction quality seems very good, especially the cord (a common point of failure for me with any type of earphones). It comes with the regular and mini size plugs.

The sound quality is absolutly top-notch. I'm not an audiophile, so I can't throw out the phrases and jargon I typically read in audio discussion boards and magazines (well, I can throw them out, but not with any semblance of knowing what I'm taking about). So suffice it to say that I can't imagine anyone not being very pleased with the quality of sound using these and a MP3 player or an iPad (the two devices I've used with them so far). I've been absolutely amazed at how great these sound.

My only complaint is the lack of sound isolation. Outside sounds can easily be heard. Sometimes that's good, but most of the time I prefer to be isolated from whatever else is playing in the house. I'm finding I reach for these more often when I'm in a quiet environment, and use ear buds when there's a lot of noise about (with me defining noise as any type of music I don't care for).

With the caveat of the lack of sound blocking, these should absolutely be on your short list if you're looking for a comfortable, great sounding pair of earphones.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory

text_fidelity_a:
HomeScreen (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Dual Band Wireless Router/Range Extender AC750 (802.11ac) I received this as a review sample and even though I am experienced with setting up and configuring networks, this was so easy that I honestly believe anyone can set it up with the scant instructions.

My initial set up was to connect it to my DSL modem just to check it out. Although the instructions are terse, you do need to read them regardless of level of experience. For one thing, it requires you to completely power off your broadband modem. For another, it takes a bit to boot up no matter how you intend to use it. Connecting to broadband was a snap.

What I really wanted was a range extender and this was as simple to configure for that as it was to configure for broadband. In that mode, when you first power it on and boot up it takes over a minute and you may be tempted to think it's broken. Don't. Once it is powered up, like the broadband set up (DSL or cable), the wizard makes it simple to discover your wireless router, connect to it and extend the range of your network. My wireless router turns in a weak -70dB from my master bedroom (measured with [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]]) and once I installed this in the same room the signal dramatically improved to a strong -40dB. In the same room with my master wireless router this comes in at -47dB while the master router measures in at -56dB. That indicates that the signal of this router is exceptionally strong.

There are options for adding sensors for home control. I did not test that set of features because I did not receive sensors, but it is functionality that makes this router/extender a great choice if you do want to pursue home control too. There are IOS and Android apps that can be used in conjunction with the sensor features. Again, I did not explore those and probably will not since I am not interested in them. As a router alone I love this, and especially the overall signal strength and ease of setting up and configuring.

PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV If you read the product description carefully, you won't waste time (as I did) trying to use this PLAYSTATION 4 UNIVERSAL MEDIA REMOTE to navigate PS4 games (e.g., Journey, Minecraft). The PS4 remote uses Bluetooth to turn your PS4 on and off, and to control and navigate PS4 media (e.g., DVDs), but only controls PS4 media. The PS4 remote can also be programmed to turn your TV, Cable Box, and Audio Receiver on and off, and to control and navigate those devices (assuming they accept remote Bluetooth operation).

The PS4 remote performs the advertised functions very well, and I'm happy with it. The main thing I wanted was the PS4 on/off feature, so that I wouldn't have to fool with the skinny button on the PS4 box when I wanted to play a DVD. But I also wanted something that would make it easier to navigate DVDs. I'm not much of a gamer, and I find the game controllers awkward to use. With the PS4 remote, the forward, back, play, and arrow buttons work "normally" (like any TV remote).

NOTE THAT once the PS4 remote is paired, you will turn the playstation "on" by pressing the big PS4 button, but you will turn it "off" by navigating to the PS4's power settings (in the display). (The PS4 remote doesn't have a "sources" button for bringing up the output options on my Samsung Smart TV, so I still need a second remote for selecting the PS4 output.)

The Bluetooth pairing and setup for the PS4 remote is straightforward, but you need to follow the directions in the accompanying booklet "to the letter". You have to visit several locations in the PS4 settings to add the remote to the PS4 device list, and then complete the setup.

Programming the remote to turn on another device (TV, Cable Box, Amplifier, etc.) is exactly the same as programming any universal remote. You turn on the device you're programming, put the remote into learning mode, point it at the device, and wait for the remote to find, recognize, and turn off the device. If the remote doesn't recognize the device, you must perform the device code programming manually (lots of codes are listed in the instruction booklet). The PS4 remote recognized my TV without difficulty, but my sound bar required manual programming.

Once you've programmed the various other devices, you switch between those devices by pressing the little labeled buttons (PS4, TV, AMP, CBL). Which brings me to the only thing that I don't like about the PS4 remote--the buttons (especially the switching buttons) are quite small, because there are so many of them packed onto this rather narrow remote.
text_fidelity_b: PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV

text_fidelity_a:
Cobra RX680 Waterproof Walkie Talkies for Adults - Rechargeable, 60 Preset Channels, Long Range 38-Mile Two-Way Radio Set (2-Pack),Black and Orange So many things I love about these. These appear to be as rugged and well built as I'd expected from a brand name like Cobra. I love that they include a flashlight, and especially that the units are USB rechargeable! Such a convenient way to power things these days, I wish more electronics ditched the AAA batteries thing like this!
The range might be a bit exaggerated, but to be fair I live in a very wooded area surrounded by hills and valleys. I found that around my neighborhood it worked great but if I went a few miles away, the sound was mostly just unintelligible crackling. We could still hear that someone was trying to say something, but that's it.
On the flip side, we started hearing someone else's conversation the next day... we were just testing it so we didn't bother changing the default channel, and it turns out someone else must have gotten some talkies on the same default frequencies. I have no idea how close they were, but my kids pointed out that someone was talking and we didn't press any buttons and then we all heard it. "Dad? Do I need to come in? I'm playing outside", and then a few seconds later "ok, but don't ride into the street". Then some clicks of singing and other noises- clearly someone else communicating with THEIR kid was coming through to us. I pressed the talk button and said "Hi- this is the default frequency for these walkie talkies, so we should both probably change them!" and then promptly picked another channel. So, that's kind of neat because I have no idea where these other people were, we live in a pretty urban area with houses spread out and I know it wasn't someone from my block. Yet we heard them clear as day. So, I'd say these are pretty good at what they do, but maybe don't rely on the full extent of their listed range.
text_fidelity_b: Cobra RX680 Waterproof Walkie Talkies for Adults - Rechargeable, 60 Preset Channels, Long Range 38-Mile Two-Way Radio Set (2-Pack),Black and Orange

I tried this camera as well as the Sony RX10 at my local camera store. The Panasonic has a noticeably longer zoom range, but the long end is much slower than the RX10, which makes your images noticeably worse in lower light conditions (like inside a camera store or any indoor conditions). The Panasonic is noticeably bulkier in your hand (about half an inch bigger in all dimensions). One comparison that the specs don't really tell you is that the build quality is significantly worse in the Panasonic compared to the Sony. The Sony RX10 has a metal frame and weather sealed shell and better overall fit-and-finish than the Panasonic. The poorer build quality of the Panasonic is reflected in the price, so you get what you pay for. Casual photographers may be happy with the Panasonic, but regular users will probably be happier with the Sony's more durable construction.

text_fidelity_a:
COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019 This keyboard is impressive. I'm using it with my iPad air 3 and its a perfect fit. The plastic is a little stiffer than some of the softer cases available, so getting the tablet to pop in and out requires a little extra effort and care, but once in, its solidly held in place and the whole thing seems very sturdy. When closed, it seems to offer very good protection, although, with the stiffer plastic, I suppose the case itself could potentially crack if subject to overly rough treatment.

As for the keyboard, it operates independently of the tablet... that is to say, it has its own on-off switch and it must be charged separately (in addition to the tablet). Since it connects via Bluetooth, it really doesn't need to be physically attached to work, just within Bluetooth range. (You could leave your iPad on a stand while typing on the keyboard in your lap, for example).

The keys themselves feel good, with adequate travel and response to the touch - you can actually "type" on it... although it is slightly smaller than a standard keyboard (as you would expect), its still comfortable enough for regular use. Also, there's a backlight for the keys which I kinda like... my laptop also has that feature and it makes it usable anytime, anywhere (out on the deck after the sun goes down, for example).

The fact that it can be twisted around and folded back on itself for simple tablet use makes it that much more usable. It does add a little heft to an iPad air, including some weight and some thickness, so if the thin form factor and light weight were key reasons for choosing the Ipad Air in the first place, this will negate some of that.

Personally, I like this keyboard - I intend to use it when traveling instead of lugging along my oversized laptop. Recommended.
text_fidelity_b: COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019
