I like that the back pack straps tuck away so flatly and completely that it looks like a sleeve and doesn't look or feel clunky. You won't notice the straps until you decide to use them. There is also a strap for sliding over luggage handle.

It fits my 14" laptop with a little room left over. When kept as a sleeve (and not opened into the bigger bag option), I can tuck my mouse and charging cord in with the lap top.

The interior is soft and padded and is about what I expect from a sleeve, maybe even more secure. No issues.

There are two front zipper pockets while it is in the sleeve configuration.

An option to unzip a compartment that makes it into a bigger bag (or backpack) then provides even more space and storage options. Including two mesh side pockets for water bottles or whatever. Additional storage isn't significant, but it is functional. Can easily be used as a day bag (pack some snacks, and few other essentials), maybe pushing it as an overnight bag (unless super minimalist), but it is definitely great as a sleeve that can be opened up to carry more treasures. Doubt I would have used this as my high school or college pack pack because I usually carried a lot, and I dont think this will carry much more than a book or two. It simply isn't a traditional back pack, but I dont think you would be looking at this if that is what you were after.

The material has a smooth canvas feel. Very clean lines. Minimalist look. I have this in wine red, and it a great color.

I like it, and it is much nicer, sturdier, and attractive than I expected.

Unless it falls apart on me soon, I see no reason not to give it full rating. If I experience anything else, I will be back to update.

"Slim & Expandable Design: Slim style for light travel and commute, 200% Expandability when more belongings and easily to switch between the both."

TP-Link WiFi 6 AX3000 PCIe WiFi Card (Archer TX3000E), Up to 2400Mbps, Bluetooth 5.2, 802.11AX Dual Band Wireless Adapter with MU-MIMO,OFDMA,Ultra-Low Latency, Supports Windows 11, 10 (64bit) only Upgrading to this card gave my aging PC a nice boost in performance for both wifi and bluetooth. My previous wireless card was an ASUS one which only supported wireless-N, so several generations out of date. For some reason I never upgraded the wifi card on my PC even though I got a new router last year, so upgrading to this gave me a notable boost in performance as well as getting better signal strength.

Also love that this has bluetooth built in, I previously had a dongle bluetooth adapter on the PC and this one performs much better, again improved signal strength and no dropouts.

The only downsides to this wifi card are that the pigtail cables which connect the antenna may be short for some scenarios (if you don't want to place it right on top of your PC case or you have a very large one). And also its a new chipset with drivers that may still have some kinks to work out.. they have released updates recently which fix the main issue I was having though (occasional wifi dropouts) so hopefully it remains stable.

Nikon D810 FX-format Digital SLR Camera Body I have had this camera since July 2015 and I find that this camera to be the most incredible camera I have ever owned. However, the D810 is very demanding on lenses. Inferior lenses will provide either inconsistent performance, or just plain horrendous results.

Nor do I understand why some people complain about the fact that most of the outer shell is made of carbon fiber. For years I worked with advanced composites, and carbon fiber is not just cheap plastic, but is used in many high-tech products for its superior strength and light weight.
I can only speak from my own experience and knowledge.

Kindle Fire HDX 7", HDX Display, Wi-Fi and 4G LTE, 16 GB - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 3rd) I love it! This is a replacement for my Nook HD. I think it's still useful and I still like it, but I wanted something with better specs. After some research, I chose the Kindle HDX. I like that it's built right in to be able to download from 3rd party - something that isn't easily done on a Nook. I love how the reader learns your reading speed and tells you how long it will take you to read each chapter or finish the book (Nook doesn't have it).

I considered Nexus or other pure android tablets, but Fires have better specs and for a cheaper price, with ad support. There is some bloatware, but it's minimal. I don't have to have Facebook and Twitter taking up space if I don't want them to.

In my opinion, the only con is not being able to use googleplay natively. Most things that you can get from google play, the amazon app store has an alternative or you can get an apk from elsewhere. However, I paid for AVG for tablets through googleplay, but can't use it now unless I pay for it again. The tablet game I play (Legion of Heroes) isn't in the app store yet (though it's coming). For right now, I can play my googleplay movies on my Fire, but when I sell or give away my Nook, will I still be able to access my content?

There are workarounds to get some google play stuff to work without rooting, but not paid apps and not in game purchases. You can't link your Fire to the googleplay store so if it's your only device, you're out of luck.

Fire would be the best all around tablet, if amazon and google play would learn to play nicely with each other and share. Still, I highly recommend Fire HDX

Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version) I have had these for a day. They are absolutely amazing. Life changing, worth every penny. I have seen a lot of reviews where they were compared to AirPods Pros, but there is no comparison.

I bought them because I have a noisy (but lovable) neighbor. The noise cancellation on these is superior, but not for low, bassy, external sounds, but rather sounds in the higher range.

My advise, and to save you some time: Do not get the app. It is so invasive of your information, and I know all apps are, but this one is probably the worst. You can set up bluetooth with all your devices without the app, and use all the features, no problem.

It also has Alexa built in, which is insane, I have yet to pull the trigger on giving Alexa permission, but I think I will; there is an Alexa button, I THINK that's the only time it's listening. If you're like me, and you have Amazon Prime Music the combo is insane.

A few cons: the Noise Cancellation will pound your ears if you’re not listening to content. I didn’t know it could do this, but I can see why people say they can only wear them for so long.

Do not under any circumstance get the app. It’s much more invasive than any app I’ve seen (of tkunborher to read the privacy (publicity) statement. Your earphones can operate fine without the app.

text_fidelity_a:
eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee I contacted Eufy after the battery died after 4 weeks. Took them 2 days to send me an autobot emailed response to which I responded that I wanted a live person to email me. Another 2 days, and a person asked me to send a screen shot of the battery settings. REALLY??? So I did that which my battery settings were for optimized battery life. Another 2 days and still no answer. There was an option on the bottom of their email to escalate the case to management if I was not happy with the response, and that they would get back to me within 24 hours. So I clicked it, and explained how I was not getting a response. But guess what? I never got a response. So five days later, I decided to return this because I'm still in the return window. Maybe I had a defective unit. We have had a very mild winter, so I cannot imagine that the weather would make a supposed four-month battery charge only last for four weeks. Plus, there isn't much motion going on to drain the battery either. Sometimes, 3 or 4 days go by with no motion. The most number of times it has detected motion in one day is four times. So it's not like the battery is getting drained from the camera being triggered 10 times a day. I'm going to try one more time, and watch the battery life to see how quickly it drains before the return window closes.

**** Update **** The replacement camera will have a battery life of approximately 6 or 7 weeks, judging by the amount of battery used thus far. Since the return window is just 4 weeks, I have returned this camera again and will not try another one. 6-7 weeks battery life is better than 4 weeks, for sure. But still disappointing because Eufy advertises a 4 month battery life. I would have been willing to try to Eufy 2 Pro that has a 365-day battery life (figuring it probably really only has a 6 month battery life). But this would mean purchasing a home base. Also, the location of the camera does not get any direct sunlight, so even a solar panel would not have helped. If you are looking for just one camera that is wireless, and you aren't interested in having to take it down every month or two for recharging, this is not the camera for you. Their customer support contacted me the day after I wrote my first review. (I couldn't get any support previously through their normal channels.)
text_fidelity_b: eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WHXB900N Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset - Blue (Amazon Exclusive) Sony WH-XB900N Wireless Noise Canceling Extra Bass Headphones have great sound quality. Plus, for an over the ear headphone they are surprisingly lightweight. I also like how they bend to fold up and are really pliable. However, that's really where the greatness stops. Pairing these with any device I own is difficult or doesn't happen at all. These will not pair with my laptop. My laptop sees it's there. It claims it's playing from the headphones, but alas it does not most of the time. In addition, these will not play from iTunes. So, if you have an Apple device forget it. These will not pair with my iPhone 5. For two reasons, first, these are terrible with Apple devices/software and second, you must have the App to pair the headphones, which if you have an older phone won't happen because the App is only compatible with certain iOS systems. As much as I am angry with Apple for stopping all updates for older Apple devices (which work just fine otherwise), it's equally frustrating with App developers who do not design their Apps to be compatible with the older systems. So, most of my experience with these headphones is through the AUX jack.

Therefore, the sound quality is really good. I listen to a lot of hiphop and the bass is spot on. However, I do listen other types of music (pretty much everything) and I would have to say listening to Beethoven's 6th and Old Blind Dogs was a nice experience as well! The noise cancelling is a joke. I can hear everything around me still. In fact, I'm currently wearing these as I type this review and can hear the click clack of the keys, my son bump around upstairs, and my father just call my name. So, if you wear these on public transportation or at work, you're gonna hear everything as usual. But they are good headphones and comfortable on my ears.

The instructions are ridiculous. Can we stop with the picture instructions? They make no sense. I need words and should not have to depend on internet video reviews to get clarity on how to use anything. There is a way to play, pause, volume down/up by tapping or swiping, but I have no idea how to do it. Sometimes it works, sometimes not. They have a long battery life. I charged these weeks ago and they still have a charge as I use them now.

So, these have a great sound quality, the noise cancellation doesn't do anything, and you need to pair these with non-Apple devices.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WHXB900N Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset - Blue (Amazon Exclusive)
